doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Working with the masters before leading, and Flying Dutchman
summary: He waited for opportunity, hung out with Monk, then joined Miles; earlier he recorded for Bob Thiele with Pharoah Sanders and Gato Barbieri.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I was thinking the other day about in the 80s they had this term in jazz, the “young lions.” We had a lot of young guys coming up, and they were making albums as leaders when they were in their early 20s. You were like 33 I think when you became a leader.
Okay. Did you, how should I say this, did you wait on purpose or were you just waiting for the opportunity?

I guess waiting for opportunity because I was — I mean I just loved music. So I was playing, — when I left home I said I want to work with all the masters. And so I worked with Max, I worked with Art Blakey, and I think he did something with Mingus. So I met all of them, so when I was with Art Blakey I had a chance to hang out with Monk one night. Monk came down to hang out with Art, so I hung out with Monk and that was a pleasant surprise because you know everyone was saying Monk is so eccentric, but man, shoot, Monk talked for about 24 hours.
